Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions); Raj Patel (CTO, Pinegrove), Lina Zhou (Platform), Samir Khan (Security), Jules (ML)
summary: Initial migration discovery for moving from hosted OpenAI + in-house vLLM inference into a combination of Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Key concerns: eval parity with TGI/vLLM baseline, latency vs cost tradeoffs, VPC/on-prem constraints, SOC2 and KMS integration. Customer is leaning toward a pilot on Redwood Dedicated with potential Private deployment later for regulated customers.
topics: Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Operational concerns: KV cache, batching, model variants
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. We're here to understand Pinegrove's path off your current mix of OpenAI plus an in‑house vLLM cluster and to talk options — hosted, dedicated, private. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Raj Patel: Yeah, Raj here. CTO. We've got Jules on ML, Lina on infra, Samir on security. Our main thing is we need to stop paying for two different patterns and also get predictable latency.
[00:00:27] Lina Zhou: we run an on prem-ish vLLM farm for burst and use OpenAI for prod serving, obv cost is spiking, and the telemetry is fragmented.
[00:00:40] Maya Chen: cool, thanks. can you remind us what your average request size and latencies look like? token sizes, concurrency?
[00:00:52] Jules: typical prompts 120-300 tokens, about 700 QPS during peak for light assistant traffic, but napkin burst to 1.5k for analytics queries. latency SLO is 200ms P95 ideally but we tolerate up to 500ms for complex runs.
[00:01:10] Alex Moreno: okay that's helpful. A couple quick follow-ups: are you using KV cache today in your vLLM setup? and are you doing quantized models for cost?
[00:01:22] Jules: yeah KV cache via homegrown shards, and we've tried int8 in vLLM for some models, not all. TGI is used for some conv stacks, but parity isn't perfect — sometimes outputs drift.
[00:01:36] Raj: exactly, eval parity with TGI/vLLM is the blocker. We need to match quality with less ops overhead. also security — some customers require data residency and KMS integration.
[00:01:48] Samir Khan: on security, SOC 2 is table stakes; we also need SSO/SAML, RBAC, HSM/KMS, audit logs and retention controls. plus we need a clear exit playbook.
[00:02:00] Maya Chen: totally reasonable. Redwood supports SAML/SSO and KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated, and audit logs with retention policy. For exit, we provide request level logs and model versioning to reproduce outputs — we'll show the runbook.
[00:02:18] Raj: good. can you walk us through how you'd preserve parity — like, what does the eval process look like?
[00:02:26] Diego Ramos: sure. typical approach: we baseline your prompts against your vLLM/TGI stack — exact prompt set, temperature, sampling settings. we run side‑by‑side inference with matching tokenization and model weights where possible, capture outputs, and run your scoring metrics. then we iterate on quantization/sequence length and kernel selection to close gaps.
[00:02:45] Jules: do you run this on our private infra or on Redwood hosted? we want to avoid leaking data.
[00:02:52] Maya Chen: we can run benchmarks in a few ways: 1) your environment — we provide a test harness you run locally, 2) Redwood Dedicated in an isolated tenant with synthetic but representative data, or 3) Private deployment in your VPC or on‑prem if you need no data egress.
[00:03:08] Lina Zhou: perfect. how about performance tuning — batching and caching — we need throughput for the analytics queries and low tail latency for assistant traffic.
[00:03:17] Maya Chen: Redwood's serving runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache optimizations. For Dedicated, we can tune batch windows and kernel selection based on your sequence length distribution. For low latency paths we recommend a small dedicated pool pinned to low batch sizes plus prefix caching.
[00:03:34] Raj: and costs — how do you model token costs vs dedicated commits? we need predictable unit economics.
[00:03:40] Alex Moreno: pricing flows two ways: hosted usage-based per token/embedding; dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with committed throughput and lower per-token economics. for customers with bursty peaks we add burst capacity. we'll share a cost model sheet.
[00:03:55] Samir Khan: encryption — how is KV cache encrypted and can keys be customer-managed?
[00:04:01] Maya Chen: yes, customer KMS allowed for Dedicated and Private. KV cache is encrypted at rest; we can enable HSM for private deployments on request.
[00:04:12] Jules: what about fallback? if you don't have a particular model compiled or capacity is full, do you auto-fallback to a smaller model? we tried that once and it produced nonsense.
[00:04:21] Diego Ramos: we have smart routing policies with canary/fallbacks but you control the policies. you can set automatic fallback to model variants with guardrails or return a 429 so you can retry. we recommend automated A/B only after verifying eval parity.
[00:04:36] Raj: are there known gotchas migrating from OpenAI to Redwood hosted? tokenization differences, sampling?
[00:04:44] Maya Chen: tokenization is consistent if you use the same tokenizer weights; sampling defaults differ so we advise normalizing temperature/seed and running a parity test. sometimes function calling semantics need minor adapter code.
[00:04:57] Lina Zhou: on networking, if we go Dedicated but keep traffic inside our VPC, is there a VPN or private link option?
[00:05:04] Alex Moreno: yes, Dedicated can be fronted by PrivateLink or an IPsec tunnel. for Private deployments we hand over control plane and you run the runtime in your VPC.
[00:05:14] Samir Khan: contractually, can we get SLAs for latency percentiles for Dedicated?
[00:05:19] Diego Ramos: we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on Dedicated with commit levels; specifics depend on pool size and topology. we'll map your SLOs to sizing.
[00:05:30] Jules: curious re model compilation — do you support quantized kernels for Mistral/GPT‑like models?
[00:05:36] Maya Chen: yes, we have quantization-friendly execution paths and kernel selection logic by architecture. Mistral and GPT family variants are supported with int8/4 options depending on model.
[00:05:47] Raj: what's the typical timeline for a pilot if we want Dedicated plus an eval parity sprint?
[00:05:52] Alex Moreno: timeline usually: week 0 kickoff, week 1 collect prompts and test harness, week 2 run baselines, week 3 iterate on tuning, week 4 present parity report. Dedicated pilot provisioning can take 1–2 weeks depending on cloud region and GPU inventory.
[00:06:08] Lina Zhou: inventory concerns — what GPU types do you use? we prefer A100s for float workloads but also look at H100 for throughput.
[00:06:14] Diego Ramos: we support both A100 and H100 pools. Dedicated lets you pin instance types; Private is whatever you provision.
[00:06:22] Samir Khan: documentation — we need SOC2 docs, architecture diagrams, pen test results.
[00:06:27] Alex Moreno: we'll share our security pack — SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, pen test summary, KMS integration docs and a draft data processing addendum.
[00:06:36] Raj: are there customers who've done an OpenAI + vLLM consolidation onto Redwood? any case studies?
[00:06:42] Maya Chen: yes, a few customers moved from hybrid OpenAI + in-house vLLM to Dedicated — win on cost predictability and lowered ops. I'll send a short case note and the benchmark spreadsheet.
[00:06:53] Jules: can we run a micro benchmark for our prompt set on your infra? we want to compare P95 and log‑loss.
[00:06:59] Maya Chen: absolutely. Maya: we'll need your prompt set, expected traffic profile, and the scoring script. we'll run vLLM baseline side‑by‑side and share raw outputs.
[00:07:12] Raj: regarding versioning, how do you pin model versions and reproduce outputs for audits?
[00:07:17] Diego Ramos: model registry with immutable version hashes, seedable samplers, and exportable run artifacts. we can hand over snapshots for audits and reproduce inference with the same kernel/quantization settings.
[00:07:30] Alex Moreno: quick note on costs — we also recommend caching static responses and embedding caches for similarity retrieval to reduce token spend.
[00:07:38] Lina Zhou: agreed that's low hanging fruit.
[00:07:41] Samir Khan: one last security question: if we do hybrid (some customer data on private nodes, others on hosted), can we route requests by tenant?
[00:07:49] Maya Chen: yes, per-tenant routing policies supported; you can route sensitive tenants to Private or Dedicated pools and keep others on Hosted.
[00:07:58] Raj: good. ok next steps then — we want pricing, security pack, and a plan for the parity sprint.
[00:08:05] Alex Moreno: noted. i'll send the pricing matrix and draft SOW. Maya will own the parity test and bench. Diego will size Dedicated options.
[00:08:14] Jules: timeline wise if we get pricing by Friday we can approve pilot budget next week.
[00:08:20] Alex Moreno: great. any other open Qs?
[00:08:22] Samir Khan: maybe one more — in the parity run, if outputs drift, will you postmortem and tune quantization?
[00:08:29] Maya Chen: yes we'll do iterative tuning: adjust quantize settings, kernel selection, maybe slightly change beam/search settings to match distributions. we'll log diffs and action items.
[00:08:40] Raj: perfect. thanks everyone.
[00:08:43] Alex Moreno: thanks all. we'll follow up with the items we listed. Bye.
[00:08:48] (meeting ends — rest of recording contains brief admin chat)
notes: Call was discovery with AE+SE. Customer is moderately mature (in‑house vLLM + OpenAI). Primary blockers: eval parity and security/compliance. Customer leaning Dedicated pilot followed by Private for regulated tenants. Agreed next week security deep dive and parity sprint kickoff.
recording_quality_observations: Some crosstalk and a few mis‑transcribed technical terms (TGI sometimes transcribed as T G I, vLLM as v l l m), speaker labels occasionally generic. Overall medium fidelity for automated action item extraction.
